Getting started

getting-started.Rmd

fcutils is a set of functions for the time series work behind UHERO’s forecasts. A forecast at UHERO starts from the history of many series, such as payroll jobs or visitor arrivals. Each series is then extended to a date some years ahead, using assumptions about growth or levels. The results are summarised as annual averages, growth rates, tables and plots. fcutils covers each of those steps: getting data, converting between formats and frequencies, extending series into the forecast period, and showing the results.

This article covers what every script needs first: the bank options, the data formats the functions accept, series names and how to write dates. Building a forecast and Growth rates, tables and plots follow on from it.

Install the package from GitHub:

remotes::install_github("UHERO/fcutils")
library(fcutils)

The bank

A forecast holds many series, and they need to share the same dates so that they can be added, divided and compared. fcutils calls that common date range the bank: it runs from the start of the history to the end of the forecast period. make_xts(), addf(), extend() and span(extend = TRUE) return series that cover the whole bank, and they read its first and last date from two options. Set them once at the top of a script, before calling any of these functions:

options(
  fcutils.bnk_start = as.Date("1990-01-01"),
  fcutils.bnk_end = as.Date("2035-12-31")
)

Without the options, those functions stop with an error saying so. make_xts() builds an empty or constant series on the bank, or a series from a vector of values:

make_xts(per = "quarter", val = 0) |> head(3)
#>            value
#> 1990-01-01     0
#> 1990-04-01     0
#> 1990-07-01     0
make_xts(2024.1, per = "quarter", val = c(1.5, 1.7, 1.6))
#>            value
#> 2024-01-01   1.5
#> 2024-04-01   1.7
#> 2024-07-01   1.6

Data formats

R holds time series in several ways, and fcutils takes most of them. A wide data frame has a time column and one column per series. A long data frame stacks the series in three columns, id (the series name), time and value. An xts object is a matrix of values with dates attached to the rows, from the xts package; it is convenient for arithmetic and for subsetting by date. The functions accept all of these, along with anything else that the tsbox package reads, such as base R’s ts. They return the result in the format of the input.

The package ships three wide tibbles of Hawaii data from UDAMAN, UHERO’s data system: quarterly_data_example (payroll jobs by industry, 1998–2025, in thousands), monthly_data_example (visitor arrivals and related series, in thousands) and daily_data_example (visitor arrivals by day, 2020–2022).

q <- quarterly_data_example[, c("time", "E_NF_HI", "ECT_HI")]
tail(q, 3)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   time       E_NF_HI ECT_HI
#>   <date>       <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 2024-07-01    640.   39.6
#> 2 2024-10-01    643.   39.1
#> 3 2025-01-01    648.   39.4

agg() averages quarters to years. Given a wide tibble it returns a wide tibble, and given xts it returns xts:

agg(q) |> tail(3)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   time       E_NF_HI ECT_HI
#>   <date>       <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 2022-01-01    618.   37.2
#> 2 2023-01-01    632.   38.1
#> 3 2024-01-01    639.   39.2
agg(conv_xts(q)) |> tail(3)
#>             E_NF_HI   ECT_HI
#> 2022-01-01 618.0704 37.17124
#> 2023-01-01 632.2629 38.10377
#> 2024-01-01 639.0901 39.17640

conv_long(), conv_wide(), conv_xts() and conv_tslist() convert between formats. Unlike tsbox::ts_long(), conv_long() takes wide data frames and gives a single series an id column:

conv_long(q) |> head(3)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   id      time       value
#>   <chr>   <date>     <dbl>
#> 1 E_NF_HI 1998-01-01  531.
#> 2 E_NF_HI 1998-04-01  531.
#> 3 E_NF_HI 1998-07-01  533.
conv_long(conv_xts(q)$E_NF_HI) |> head(3)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   id      time       value
#>   <chr>   <date>     <dbl>
#> 1 E_NF_HI 1998-01-01  531.
#> 2 E_NF_HI 1998-04-01  531.
#> 3 E_NF_HI 1998-07-01  533.

Series names

The examples use UHERO’s series names. A name is a mnemonic for the concept, an @, the geography and a frequency: E_NF@HI.Q is nonfarm payroll jobs (E_NF) in Hawaii (HI), quarterly (Q). When fcutils downloads a series it drops the frequency and replaces @ with _, so the column is called E_NF_HI. The series used below are:

Name Series
E_NF_HI nonfarm payroll jobs, all industries
ECT_HI construction jobs
EAF_HI accommodation and food services jobs
EGV_HI government jobs
VISNS_HI visitor arrivals, not seasonally adjusted (NS)

Dates

Wherever a function takes a date, to_ymd() reads it. A year, a quarter or a day can be a number or a string; as a number, a quarter is either a decimal (2024.3) or six digits (202403). A month must be a string, because R stores 2024.10 and 2024.1 as the same number.

to_ymd(c("2024", "2024Q3", "2024M10", "2024-10-15"))
#> [1] "2024-01-01" "2024-07-01" "2024-10-01" "2024-10-15"
to_ymd(c(2024, 2024.3, 202403, 20241015))
#> [1] "2024-01-01" "2024-07-01" "2024-07-01" "2024-10-15"

p() turns two dates into the range string that xts uses for subsetting. A year or a quarter given as the end is included in full:

x <- conv_xts(q)$E_NF_HI
x[p(2024.2, 2024)]
#>             E_NF_HI
#> 2024-04-01 636.4715
#> 2024-07-01 639.7316
#> 2024-10-01 643.2565

span() cuts any format to a range. find_start() and find_end() give the first and last date with a value:

span(q, 2024) |> head(3)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   time       E_NF_HI ECT_HI
#>   <date>       <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 2024-01-01    637.   38.9
#> 2 2024-04-01    636.   39.2
#> 3 2024-07-01    640.   39.6
find_end(q)
#> [1] "2025-01-01" "2025-01-01"

With extend = TRUE, span() also pads a series with NA out to the end of the range, which is how a series is fitted to the bank:

span(x, 2024.4, 2025.4, extend = TRUE)
#>             E_NF_HI
#> 2024-10-01 643.2565
#> 2025-01-01 647.9022
#> 2025-04-01       NA
#> 2025-07-01       NA
#> 2025-10-01       NA

Getting data

These functions need network access and keys, so this page does not run them.

get_series() downloads series from UDAMAN, UHERO’s data system, by name. get_series_exp() downloads every series in a UDAMAN export. Both need the UDAMAN token, stored once with set_udaman_token() (or as udaman_token in .Renviron), and the UHERO VPN unless public = TRUE.

get_series(c("VISNS@HI.M", "E_NF@HI.Q"))
get_series_exp(74, format = "xts")

get_series_src() downloads from FRED, Statistics Canada, the Bank of Canada, Japan’s e-Stat and the EIA. FRED, e-Stat and the EIA need a key, stored with set_api_key() or in .Renviron (FRED_API_KEY, ESTAT_API_KEY, EIA_API_KEY):

get_series_src("UNRATE", "fred")
get_series_src(c("PAYEMS", "CPIAUCSL"), "fred", format = "xts")
